Assets are loaded through provider APIs using portable resource paths.

```scala
val player = Graphics.loadImage(MultiDPIResourcesRoot / "player.png")
val music = Audio.loadMusic(ResourcesRoot / "audio" / "theme.ogg")
```

Prefer declaring assets in Bazel app rules so each backend receives the correct resource layout.

Audio is exposed through `AudioProvider`.

```scala
val sound = Audio.loadSound(ResourcesRoot / "audio" / "beep.wav")
if sound.isLoaded then sound.value.get.get.play()
```

Use short `Sound` assets for effects and `Music` for long streamed background tracks.

Application lifecycle, providers, modules, and engines.

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

SGL lets you start small with the core `Application` frame loop, then move to an engine when your game needs more structure.

```scala
trait AbstractApp extends Application {
  this: CanvasProvider with WindowProvider =>

  override def frame(dt: Double): Unit =
    withFrameCanvas { canvas =>
      canvas.drawRect(0, 0, Window.width, Window.height, Graphics.defaultPaint)
    }
}
```

<Aside type="tip" title="Pick one architecture">
Use core Canvas/OpenGL directly, or choose one primary engine: screen2d, ECS, or GameObject.
</Aside>

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

SGL supports low-level Canvas rendering, low-level OpenGL/WebGL rendering, and higher-level engine renderers.

```scala
withFrameCanvas { canvas =>
  val paint = Graphics.defaultPaint.withColor(Graphics.Color.rgb(255, 80, 120))
  canvas.drawRect(32, 32, 128, 64, paint)
}
```

<Aside type="caution">
The Canvas value passed to `withFrameCanvas` is only valid inside the callback. Do not store it.
</Aside>

SGL currently builds with Bazel.

```bash
git clone https://github.com/regb/scala-game-library.git
cd scala-game-library
bazel build //...
```

```bash
bazel run //examples/hello-canvas:desktop-awt
```

<Aside type="note">
Android remains separate from the Bazel build and uses the legacy SBT/Android workflow.
</Aside>
Notes for moving between APIs and engines.

Recent package conventions:

- 2D/3D math lives under `sgl.math`.
- GameObject engine packages use `sgl.engine.gameobject`.
- Engine examples use `sgl.examples.<engine>.<example>`.

When migrating from screen2d to core Canvas, replace `GameScreen` with `Application.frame` and `withFrameCanvas`.

import { Aside } from '@astrojs/starlight/components';

SGL does not currently bundle a full physics engine.

<Aside type="note">
The recommended approach is to integrate a physics library appropriate for your target platforms and keep synchronization with SGL transforms explicit.
</Aside>

For the GameObject engine, physics components can be ordinary components updated by systems.
Desktop, web, native, and mobile targets.

Supported backend families include:

- Desktop JVM with AWT Canvas
- Desktop JVM with LWJGL/OpenGL/OpenAL
- HTML5 Canvas and WebGL via Scala.js
- Desktop native via Scala Native and SDL2
- Android through the legacy Android/SBT setup

```bash
bazel build //examples/hello-canvas:desktop-awt
bazel build //examples/hello-scalagl:html5
bazel build //engines/gameobject/examples/asteroids:desktop-native
```
